newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk anti-rebel troops in buildup at Iraqi border.
newsitem.headline: Turk anti-rebel troops in buildup at Iraqi border.

text.p: Turkey has begun to build up troops along the Iraqi border, local sources said on Friday, a sign of a possible cross-border drive into northern Iraq against Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels.

"Since mid-April many soldiers, tanks and armoured vehicles have been passing through the border area," a resident in the southeastern town of Cizre, 40 km (25 miles) from the border, told Reuters by telephone.
Security officials were not immediately available to comment and the number of troops and military vehicles was not clear.
The army has denied Turkish press reports that a large cross-border incursion was imminent.

Three members of a state-paid, anti-rebel militia were killed in a clash with rebels early on Friday in Sirnak province near the Iraqi border, military officials said. No details on military or rebel casualties were given.
The Turkish government arms and pays around 70,000 people, mostly Kurds, to fight against the guerrillas.
Turkey has raided across the border in recent years against PKK bases in northern Iraq. It also uses large numbers of troops against the guerrillas in operations on its side of the border.
Northern Iraq is controlled by Iraqi Kurdish groups who took over the area after Baghdad's defeat in the 1991 Gulf War.

More than 22,000 people have been killed in 12 years of fighting between Turkish security forces and the rebels. Turkey was criticised by some of its Western allies for a six-week drive into northern Iraq involving 35,000 men in 1995.
It regularly pushes across the border in much smaller numbers.
